question: Write a precise definition of a circle. Use only the words point, plane, and distance, and words built from them.
correct_answer: A circle is the set of all points in a plane that are a given distance (the radius) from a given point in that plane (the center).
grading_note: Any equivalent wording. Essential: (1) ALL points, (2) in one plane, (3) at one fixed distance, (4) from one fixed point, the center. Not accepted: "a round shape" (not precise); leaving out the plane (that describes a sphere); "points within a distance" (that is a disk).

question: Points A and B lie on line ℓ. Which is a precise definition of segment AB?
choices: A. Every point of line ℓ | B. Point A and every point of line ℓ on the same side of A as B | C. Points A and B together with every point C of line ℓ for which AC + CB = AB | D. Every point of the plane that is closer to A than to B
correct_answer: Points A and B together with every point C of line ℓ for which AC + CB = AB
grading_note: A segment is its two endpoints and every point between them; "C is between A and B" means C is on the line and AC + CB = AB (distance along a line). The other choices describe line ℓ, ray AB, and a half-plane.
